With me this morning are Michael J. Bender, our Chief Executive Officer, and Jill Timm, our Chief Financial Officer. I will now turn the call over to Michael.

Michael J. Bender: Thank you, Trevor. Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today for Kohl's third quarter 2026 earnings conference call. Before I begin today, I want to take a moment to thank our entire team at Kohl's. Each day is an opportunity to serve our customers, and the initiatives we've outlined are focused on improving our customers' experience. We've made great progress thus far, but additional important work remains ahead. Thank you for your dedication and commitment to Kohl's. I would also like to extend a warm welcome to Ryan Waymire, who joined Kohl's as Chief Merchandising Officer at the end of September.

Since arriving, Ryan has hit the ground running, visiting stores, collaborating with his merchandising teams, connecting with vendors and brand partners, and hearing directly from our customers. We're thrilled to leverage his deep expertise and leadership as part of our executive team. Our performance in the third quarter reflects the tangible progress we are making against our strategic initiatives, highlighted by a return to top-line growth with 1.2% positive comparable sales. As we make steady progress on our strategic initiatives, our customers are responding favorably, driving broad-based improvements across the business. While this is an encouraging milestone, we know crucial work remains ahead.

Additionally, our focus on operating the business with discipline continues to pay off as we expanded our operating margin and increased earnings per share. We continue to solidify our balance sheet, and our cash generation remains strong. The progress and ongoing execution will continue to deliver a sustainable financial framework that allows us to invest in the business and return capital to shareholders through our dividend and share repurchase programs. I would also like to acknowledge that we are operating in a challenging macroeconomic environment. The core customers that we serve are facing inflationary pressures in their daily expenses that are altering their behaviors when shopping discretionary categories.

While customers have remained resilient, it is clear that they are migrating to value with their purchases. Our strategic initiatives directly address these customer priorities. As we head into the holiday, we remain dedicated to providing compelling value to our customers through our product offerings. Now let me share some additional highlights from our performance that give us confidence that we are moving in the right direction. First, every line of business delivered a positive comp. The work we focused on throughout the year to elevate product relevance for our customer is starting to pay off, with positive results across every major category: women's, men's, kids, footwear, home, and accessories.

Second, our priority brands continue to resonate with our customers and delivered a positive 3.4% comparable sales performance in the quarter. These brands play an important role in our brand portfolio and value proposition. Our By Kohl's brands provide quality products at compelling price points, which is especially important in the current economic backdrop we are operating in. Third, over the past year, we have developed strategic targeted actions to re-engage our Kohl's Card customers. This important cohort represents our most productive and loyal customer base. We have made great progress listening to this customer and delivering products and experiences that they look for when shopping at Kohl's.

This ongoing work resulted in an improved comparable sales performance to a +2.6% with our Kohl's Card customers in the quarter. Fourth, the investments we are making into our store experience are making a difference. We have made investments into brand amplification, reduced redundancy across the floor, and invested in inventory to deliver greater trip assurance and consistency across our store fleet. While early in this work, we saw our stores return to growth and deliver a 2% comparable sales increase in the third quarter. Next, let me provide details on our three key initiatives and the progress we are making to deliver a better customer experience.

Beginning with our first initiative, offering a curated and more balanced assortment that fulfills the needs of all customers. This initiative focuses on addressing customer demand by clarifying assortments, elevating product relevance, and offering the key items and categories shoppers want. While there is still more work ahead in this initiative, our work is resonating with customers in the third quarter. Every line of business improved sequentially versus prior quarter and delivered a positive comp. Starting with the women's business, we returned to growth in the third quarter with a 0.5% comparable sales increase. Strength continues to be led by our juniors business, which delivered its fourth straight quarter of high-single-digit comparable sales increases.

In addition, we showed a strong performance in our denim business, with proprietary denim up over 30% and Levi's up high-single-digits. We saw outperformance in our transition to cool weather goods with fleece and long-sleeve tees up low teens, and we expect this momentum to continue in the fourth quarter. Our intimates and sleepwear businesses were pressured in the quarter, and we continue to make progress with our reduced choice counts and improved depth, which is especially important to these categories. Moving to our men's business, which delivered a +1.5% comparable sales performance. This 240 basis point improvement from Q2 was a result of the work we have been doing to deliver a more clear and simplified shopping experience.

We've made great progress in this category, editing out redundancies and investing into key programs that resonate with our customers. A great example of this is within our FLX brand, which continues to grow at an outstanding pace and has developed into a top brand in our men's department. Within active, we've also experienced strength from Tek Gear and Nike apparel. Our dress category also delivered strong performance in the quarter, up 11%, highlighted by Haggar. Softness in the men's business was driven by sportswear, which is still in the process of editing through assortments to provide improved clarity. Now let me move to our kids business, which accelerated to a +1.3% comp in the third quarter.

Kids continues to experience outsized performance within our toys business from trending products like LEGO, KPop Demon Hunters, and NeeDoh squishies. We're well-positioned to build on this momentum as we head into the holiday season, as toys and gifting becomes a higher penetration of our business. Within kids apparel, we're seeing solid results from our fall seasonal merchandise with key brands like FLX Kids and SO. Although early, we are pleased with the initial results we saw within our baby and infant category, where we recently reintroduced the offering of our opening price point proprietary brand, Jumping Beans. Additionally, our Babies“R”Us initiative delivered another quarter of positive growth.

This September, we completed 56 additional Babies“R”Us shop build-outs and recently rolled out accessories towers in nearly all stores offering our highest velocity gifts and accessories. As we anticipated, our footwear business returned to growth in the third quarter, generating a 4% positive comp. This marks over a 700 basis point improvement from just the second quarter. Highlights include improved newness and depth in key brands like Nike, adidas, and Skechers, all delivering positive comparable sales. Additionally, we're excited about the performance we saw within our boots business, which was heavily impacted by tariffs last fall. In the third quarter, boots grew over 20% versus prior year, and we expect positive momentum in boots to continue into the fourth quarter.

Our accessories business improved and delivered a +0.7% comparable sales performance. Excluding Sephora, our accessories business maintained its mid-single-digit growth trend, led by impulse, jewelry, and luggage. Impulse continued its strong momentum, delivering more than a 20% comparable sales increase. Through this initiative, we are able to offer frequent newness and great value to our customers, featuring everyday essentials and small gifting items. Jewelry continued its momentum, achieving its second straight quarter of mid-single-digit growth. In October, we expanded elevated fashion jewelry displays and fine jewelry case lines across more than 300 locations. Looking ahead, we see further opportunity to build the presence of this important gifting category across our omnichannel platforms.

Our Sephora at Kohl's business ran down 1.9% versus prior year. Although this continues to underperform the company, the Q3 results mark a 200 basis point improvement from Q2. We experienced continued pressure in the third quarter from a few of our top brands as they recently expanded their distribution. To partially offset some of this pressure, we partnered closely with Sephora to curate an offering of differentiated products and experiences for our customers. This includes expanded gifting and value sets, new travel-sized assortments, exciting brand launches, and unlocking same-day delivery for Sephora customers by leveraging our DoorDash and Instacart partnerships.

Looking deeper, fragrance remained a bright spot in the third quarter with outperformance in key brands like YSL, KAYALI, and Valentino. Our makeup business improved from Q2 by nearly 400 basis points in the third quarter, led by the rollout of MAC to all stores, which continues to exceed our expectations. We saw additional strength from prestige brands such as Charlotte Tilbury and Merit. Skincare continues to be the biggest challenge as we lap expanded distribution headwinds. This fall, we have introduced a lot of newness in the skincare business with exciting brands like Beauty of Joseon in the K-beauty category and Salt & Stone in the body category, both of which are off to strong starts.

Home continued to improve their business in the third quarter, delivering a 1% comp increase. This performance was driven by strength in electronics and bath categories. In small electrics, we continue to see newness and innovation resonate with customers, with key national brands Shark, Ninja, and KitchenAid posting strong double-digit comparable sales increases. Within our seasonal décor business, we were able to right-size our depth and invest more into choice counts. We are pleased with the customer response in our harvest and holiday décor businesses. Next, let me move to our second initiative, re-establishing Kohl's as a leader in value and quality.

In today's environment, it is evident that our customers have become increasingly choiceful with their discretionary spending as their budgets remain under pressure. Customers are looking to stretch every dollar, and we know how important it is to meet their needs, especially this upcoming holiday season. Our goal is to firmly position Kohl's as a trusted destination where families can consistently find excellent quality and relevant styles at compelling price points. We are delivering value through several avenues in order to deepen customer engagement while also attracting new shoppers. This work begins with elevating our proprietary brand portfolio, which, as I mentioned before, delivered over 3% sales growth in the third quarter.

These brands match affordability with modern style and continue to play an essential role in our assortment. In Q3, we made further progress enhancing these brands by increasing inventory depth while also investing into the in-store experience and scaling our marketing efforts to effectively build awareness for new and existing customers. Brands like SO, FLX, and LC Lauren Conrad continue to lead our apparel assortment, while brands like Miryana and Mingle & Co. drove strong performances in home. Additionally, we continue to discover new ways to enhance our ability to connect with customers throughout their shopping journey.

This includes leveraging targeted offers to deepen our engagement with our savvy Kohl's Card customers, who love the additional discounts they receive as Kohl's most loyal shoppers. Lastly, we saw a strong response from customers during our Kohl's Deal Days event in early October. This event highlighted broader and more simplified value messaging across key brands and categories to showcase the value we are offering. We are building on this success to provide exceptional value throughout our shopping experience. Our gifting and impulse business continues to become more impactful and serves to drive incremental units in our customers' baskets.

Our toy towers and deal bars are driving momentum by providing a compelling assortment of toys and home décor at price points under $10. Finally, our back-to-school offerings included thousands of back-to-school items priced under $25 to fit all budgets, all of which delivered strong results in the third quarter. Turning to our third initiative, building a frictionless omnichannel experience. Our teams made measurable progress in the third quarter across our inventory, store experience, and digital capabilities. Starting with our inventory management and allocation, disciplined merchandise planning remains foundational to our operating model. By establishing more timely, targeted inventory flows, we drove stronger full-price sell-through across key seasonal categories, reflected in our fall seasonal business increasing low single digits.

A core component of this inventory management and allocation is tailored to deliver trip assurance. We are intentionally simplifying the shopping experience by increasing our apparel inventory depth by mid-teens while trimming total choice counts by high teens. This deliberate shift delivers improved clarity and ensures our core high-demand items are reliably in stock. In addition, we are refining our allocation algorithms to better support lower-volume stores, ensuring a more consistent shopping experience across our store fleet. While still early in this work, we are already seeing the payoff as stores delivered positive comparable sales in the quarter. Another way to support our stores is through a more elevated experience.

Our store fleet serves as a competitive advantage for Kohl's, as we are investing in an enhanced in-store environment to drive engagement and conversion. This September, we rolled out this elevated experience to nearly all of our stores, highlighting our By Kohl's brands. These dedicated areas feature upgraded outfitting mannequins, clear navigation signage, and find your fit guides that make styling and self-service easier. Additionally, we are testing a strengthened brand and storytelling presentation with key brands like Nike and Levi's. Finally, on digital modernization, we are evolving our digital ecosystem to give customers inspiration and flexibility in how they shop. We continue to be encouraged by the initial results from our Ask Kohl's agentic shopping assistant.

Customers who engaged with Ask Kohl's are finding a more personalized experience, driving higher conversion and revenue per visit. In today's retail environment, customers are prioritizing speed and convenience. To capitalize on this, we recently launched same-day delivery offerings through partnerships at DoorDash and Uber Eats to complement our Instacart partnership. We are pleased with the start of this strategy and believe there is further opportunity to leverage our large and conveniently located store base to reach our customers. Additionally, we launched Klarna earlier this month, which provides a flexible payment option for our customers. Now, I would like to provide a brief update on how we are positioned for the important holiday season.

Our focus is on solidifying Kohl's as the go-to destination for value, gifting, and convenience. Consumers remaining highly choiceful with their spending, how we show up will be even more important. Knowing this, we identified three primary areas of focus this holiday. First, offering a sharpened value in our assortment. We are meeting budget-conscious shoppers with clear, compelling value, featuring $5-$20 opening price point gifts and impulse stocking stuffers. Freshness will be front and center, with nearly half of our holiday gift shop assortment being completely new this year, with the vast majority priced under $15. At the same time, we have scaled gifting across our destination categories.

This includes expanding our fine jewelry presence, dedicated in-store toy towers featuring items under $10, and curating over 2,000 Sephora prestige beauty gifts under $30. The Sephora partnership continues to be an incredible traffic driver, bolstered this season by exciting new brand arrivals and gift sets. Second, an engaging marketing campaign. Our holiday campaign, The North Kohl's, bridges inspiring brand storytelling with purposeful basket building. In our stores, we have simplified the shopping journey by creating curated discovery hubs such as the Cozy Corner, Style Square, and Hosting Headquarters, designed to drive cross-category conversion.

Across all media channels, we are leaning into broader, simplified promotional messaging to ensure our value proposition cuts through the holiday noise, particularly during peak volume moments, including Black Friday, Cyber Week, and the post-Christmas clearance window. Third, enabling frictionless omnichannel execution. Winning the holiday season requires exceptional operational agility, and we are meeting our customers however they choose to shop by launching our new AI-powered digital shopping assistant, integrating flexible payment options at checkout, and significantly expanding same-day delivery. Furthermore, for shoppers prioritizing speed and convenience right down to the wire, most of our buy online, pick up in store orders will be fulfilled and ready within two hours straight through Christmas Eve.

We are excited about the plan we have underway, and we are ready to serve our customers this holiday season. With that, I would like to hand the call over to Jill.

Jill Timm: Thank you, Michael. During today's call, I will share further details on our third quarter and year-to-date results, provide an update on our capital allocation, and commentary around our updated fiscal year 2026 guidance. Building on Michael's remarks, Q3 represents continued progress in our business. We delivered a positive comparable sales increase of 1.2% for the quarter, reflecting solid execution across our strategic priorities. This top-line expansion was driven by positive performance in both transactions and average transaction value. ATV expanded primarily through higher units per transaction, which helped offset lower average unit retail as consumers continue to seek value price points. Year-to-date, our comparable sales have declined 0.2%.

Store sales increased 2% on a comparable basis in the third quarter, representing an acceleration of more than 400 basis points from Q2, driven by our strategic investments in inventory depth and key in-store enhancements. Conversely, digital sales declined 1% during the quarter. We delivered positive performance across all lines of business, anchored by strong momentum in our proprietary brands, which increased 3.4% in the quarter. In addition, both consumer segments strengthened in Q3, with Kohl's Card sales accelerating to a 2.6% increase and non-Kohl's Card performance improving to flat. Over the past year, we have strategically accelerated our marketplace growth to expand customer acquisition and drive top-line productivity.

By more than doubling our vendor partners, we are addressing key white space opportunities and product selection to complement our core assortment. In the third quarter, our marketplace business continued to grow and was up nearly 75% compared to last year. Including the marketplace GMV growth, our comparable sales would have improved by approximately 60 basis points and would have increased 1.8% in Q3. For the year, marketplace increased 75% and would have improved our year-to-date comp by approximately 60 basis points to up 0.3%. Other revenue, which is primarily made up of credit business, grew over 10% in the third quarter and is approximately flat year-to-date.

The main drivers of the increase was continued improvement in our Kohl's Card customer sales with outperformance over the past couple quarters, as well as improved loss rates. We now expect other revenue for the year to be up low-single-digits. Gross margin improved by 145 basis points in the third quarter. During the quarter, we received the majority of the remaining portion of our tariff refunds, bringing our total refund to approximately $190 million. We realized a benefit of $45 million from tariff refunds, driving approximately 130 basis points of gross margin benefit in Q3.

The remaining margin increase was driven by the outperformance of our proprietary brands, stronger store sales, and increased buy online, pick up in store sales, partially offset by higher fuel costs. Year-to-date gross margin increased 156 basis points, primarily driven by tariff refunds. For the year, we now expect the total gross margin benefit from tariff refunds to be approximately $160 million. SG&A expense increased in Q3 by 1.2%. As we outlined on our second quarter call, in Q3, we increased investments into store apparel and marketing to deepen customer engagement, improve customer satisfaction, and drive sales productivity. We also faced higher supply chain costs due to fuel.

These costs were partially offset by strong expense management across our corporate and credit expenses. Year-to-date, our SG&A decreased by 0.4%. Depreciation expense was $168 million in Q3 and $515 million year-to-date. Interest expense was $65 million in Q3 and $191 million year-to-date. In the third quarter, we realized a tax benefit of $137 million from the release of a tax reserve following a positive outcome on a prior period tax position. This benefited our earnings per share by $1.16 in the third quarter and $1.17 year-to-date. Our underlying effective tax rate is estimated to be 23% for the year. This resulted in net income of $254 million in Q3, or $2.15 earnings per diluted share.

During the quarter, we benefited from the sale of two of our properties, resulting in a one-time gain of $61 million and diluted earnings per share of $0.39. In addition, we also benefited from a tax reserve release of $1.16 per diluted share and a tariff refund of $0.28 per diluted share, as previously discussed. Year-to-date, our net income was $391 million, or $3.33 of earnings per diluted share. This includes one-time benefits of $1.17 per share from the tax reserve release, $0.93 from tariff refunds, and $0.39 from real estate gains. Moving on to the balance sheet and cash flow statement.

We continue to operate in a significantly better cash position compared to last year, finishing the quarter with $723 million of cash and cash equivalents. With no borrowings on our ABL, our net cash position is more than $600 million greater compared to last year. This position provides us great flexibility to invest in our business and deliver value to our customers while still returning capital to our shareholders. Inventory decreased 1% compared to last year. We continue to invest in increased apparel depth up mid-teens while reducing choice counts by high teens in Q3 to restore trip assurance for our customers.

Looking ahead, we are planning receipts up high-single-digits in the fourth quarter to support depth of our fall seasonal assortment, invest in low-volume stores, and transition goods stronger into spring. We now anticipate inventory to be flat for the year. Now I want to provide an update on our current capital allocation priorities. Our first priority will always be to invest in our business. Capital expenditures year-to-date are $253 million. Prioritizing investments in our store fleet, including brand amplification, expanding impulse lines, deploying modernized store devices and self-checkouts, as well as general maintenance projects. Additionally, we are supporting our digital business by investing in site experience, automation, and AI.

We now expect capital expenditures to total approximately $365 million-$375 million for the year. Second, we will continue to return capital to shareholders through our dividend. We returned approximately $14 million to shareholders through our dividend in the third quarter. Year-to-date, we've returned approximately $42 million. As previously disclosed, the board on November 18th declared a quarterly cash dividend of $0.125 per share payable on December 23rd. Third, we will continue to evaluate the market for opportunistic debt repurchases. We did not repurchase debt in Q3, but have bought back $113 million of debt at a discount of $15 million year-to-date.

As we continue to build our cash position, we will continue to evaluate opportunities to address long-term debt, including the 2030 notes, which become callable in June of 2027. Fourth, we will return excess capital to shareholders through our share repurchase program. As we discussed last quarter, we resumed our share repurchase program under our current $3 billion authorization, with plans to repurchase $100 million of stock in 2026. In the third quarter, we repurchased approximately $39 million. Now let me provide details on our updated guidance for 2026. Our results in Q3 directly reflect the progress we have made against our initiatives and mark an important milestone on our journey.

While we maintain confidence in our long-term strategic direction, we remain appropriately aware of the ongoing macroeconomic headwinds and evolving customer dynamics. We continue to see that customers are prudent with their spending, including being selective with discretionary expenditures, seeking out value, and leaning into promotional events. Looking ahead to the fourth quarter, we remain focused on delivering compelling value to capture customer demand throughout the holiday season. Given that context, we are raising our top- and bottom-line guidance. We now expect the following full-year GAAP outlook. Comparable sales in the range of flat to up 0.5%.

Operating margins to be in the range of 4.7%-4.9%, which includes the benefit of approximately 40 basis points from gain on real estate and approximately 100 basis points from tariff refunds. Earnings per diluted share of $4.30-$4.50, which includes the impact of $0.40 from the gain on real estate, $1.03 of tariff refunds, and $1.17 from tax benefit. This implies the following outlook for the fourth quarter. Comparable sales in the range of flat to up 2%. Operating margin in the range of 4%-4.4%, which includes approximately 25 basis points of tariff benefit. Earnings per diluted share of $0.95-$1.15, which includes a benefit of approximately $0.10 from tariff refunds.

Before we move to Q&A, I want to express my deepest appreciation to the entire Kohl's team. Your relentless focus and hard work delivered real momentum and strong progress against our key initiatives. While we have more work ahead of us, I am incredibly proud of what we have accomplished and am confident in the path forward. Thank you for your continued dedication to our customers and our business. With that, Michael and I are happy to take your questions at this time.

Charles (Chuck) Grom: Okay, that is great to hear. As we look ahead to 2027, trying to build upon some of your success so far this year, can you talk about the initiatives to improve Sephora. Michael J. Bender: Yeah. Thanks for the question, Mark. I think we're all really excited about how quickly that has snapped back. If you recall, this time last year, we were talking about that particular cohort of our customers performing not the way we wanted to. The fact that they are now up and positive is a really big testament to the work that we are doing to excite that customer about Kohl's again.

Mark R. Altschwager: Great. Congrats on the return to positive comps, and best of luck over holiday.

Operator: Your next question comes from the line of Robert (Bob) Drbul with BTIG. Your line is open. Please go ahead.

Robert (Bob) Drbul: Hi. Good morning. Just two questions from me. First, on the footwear business. Can you talk a bit more around the trends that you are seeing with the key brands that you mentioned, and I guess sort of more as you are seeing fourth quarter and into 2027 around the footwear business? Then second question is, can you expand a bit just on the performance of the digital business, as well as the digital modernization that is underway and what you are seeing within that piece of the business? Thanks.

Michael J. Bender: Yeah. I will take a shot maybe at the first question around footwear, and Jill, please chime in as well. Footwear has been an exciting turnaround category story for us, Bob, and it is 700 basis point improvement from the prior quarter and a big, big change. We had said that we would start to see that business turn around the back-to-school timeframe, and the merchant that leads that business has been spot on in terms of her expectation of that happening, and that is what we are seeing.

Obviously, we had some challenges last year with tariffs that prevented us from having a full assortment that is focused in that footwear category, but the team has worked very hard in bringing that back to life for us that is showing up in the business. Boots is a big bright spot for us going forward in that category, and we have every expectation that will continue to go forward. So, we feel good about that. As far as the digital business is concerned, we have some opportunity, we know, to continue to make that business one that contributes more to the business for us.

We are not pleased with the slowdown, but we have got a number of initiatives underway inside the business to continue to make that piece of the business continue to perform for us better. Jill, anything else you would—

Jill Timm: Yeah, I think you asked about kind of what modernization means, and I think there is a couple things. First, it is going to be a long-term play for us, Bob. This is not going to happen overnight. We brought in Arianne Parisi, and she has made a lot of quick changes. Obviously, our marketplace growth, bringing in different payment options, speed for convenience with having DoorDash, Uber Eats, Instacart. We have Ask Kohl's on the agentic commerce side, which although still small, we are meeting the customer where they want to be, and we do see that when we have them engage with Ask Kohl's, we have a higher revenue per visit.

So those are all leading indicators, I think, of why we think this business will get back to growth. But there are things like the site enhancements for just faster performance, better product experiences, improved discovery and navigation, that is going to take a longer term for us to really get back out to parity with competitors. I think in the short run, we feel great with some of the initiatives that we have in flight, but we know over the long term, we have to compete stronger here and definitely not pleased with the slowdown we saw, but feel very confident in the work and efforts we have ahead.

Robert (Bob) Drbul: Great. Thank you very much.

Operator: Your next question comes from the line of Dana Telsey with Telsey Advisory Group. Your line is open. Please go ahead.

Dana Telsey: Hi. Good morning, everyone, and so nice to see the progress. As you think about the Kohl's Card customer, one of the benefits has been the increased coupon eligibility. Where are you on that path? Are the brands you want all on there? Is there more to come? Then when you think about not just Q4, but even a framework for 2027, on the margin structure, Jill, how do you think about puts and takes, and where does freight and fuel costs land? Thank you.

Michael J. Bender: Yeah, Dana, thanks for the question. I would say on the Kohl's credit card customer, you're exactly right. The coupon eligibility has been a big driver of our ability to continue to improve that performance. We made those changes last year in two different tranches, one in April, one in August of last year. I would say we're about where we need to be at this point. As we continue to bring different brands on, we'll make that evaluation.

But we feel very good about that and the response that you're seeing in terms of that customer cohort being positive now, I think is a big testament to the fact that we listened to the customer and we built the story around making sure that we were able to bring the products that they are interested in buying from us, whether it's petites or jewelry or some of the others that are coupon-eligible brands back into the mix, and that's what's showing up.

Jill Timm: Then I think from a margin structure perspective, I definitely think, as we mentioned, when we get to a 1% comp, that's our sweet spot and when we can start leveraging and expanding our operating margin. Clearly, this is where we got to from this quarter. There will be pressures, like you mentioned, freight and fuel, but I think this company does an amazing job. They step up to the plate when we have some of these pressures. I think last year, tariffs was a specific example. You saw the sourcing team, the merchant team really come together to find a way to offset the tariff pressure, and we really didn't have that conversation last year.

Then this year, as you can see, we're letting the tariff benefit flow through. So, I would say definitely going to see it as a continued pressure, but feel good with the work the team is doing to find ways to offset some of that pressure. So, as long as it maintains where it is at, obviously it is ever-moving, I feel like we have a good plan forward, and we will obviously be able to speak more to that in detail as we give our 2027 guidance.

Operator: Your next question comes from the line of Michael Binetti with Evercore ISI. Your line is open. Please go ahead.

Michael Binetti: Guys, congrats on a great quarter. Nice to chat with you today. I guess, on Sephora for a minute, nice to see the sequential improvement there. How do you think about how the merchandise changes that you guys laid out today help with recruiting that incremental beauty customer via the assortment versus servicing existing customers that are coming in at a lower price point today? Are you seeing any changes in those dynamics as you start to see the sequential improvement in trends in 3Q? And then, to your comments about October being the best month of the quarter, I do not think we have heard that elsewhere in retail.

Can you just help us think about the better trends you saw in the South and how those categories or initiatives are starting to translate into the rest of the fleet or the other markets as we get into fourth quarter?

Michael J. Bender: Yeah, sure. On your first question about Sephora and the category alignment there, we made changes a little while ago in terms of the positioning of juniors across from Sephora, as an example. That category, as we had mentioned, has shown four straight quarters of high-single-digit improvement over the past year or so. We think that's a direct reflection of the fact that we've situated that positioning of our business across from Sephora, and we'll continue to do that. That will continue to drive the business going forward with the Sephora customer. We have seen the conversion of that customer continue to improve going forward as well, and that's something that we'll curate as we go.

Jill, I'll turn it over to you for the second question.

Jill Timm: Yeah. I love that we can be an outlier on the positive side, Michael, in terms of where October is. Definitely ending with strength and leading into November feels good. I would say a couple things there. One is we talked about our Deal Days resonated incredibly well, and that helped drive some momentum into October, which to me is always a good sentiment of what's to come, right? That's our first step into really from a holiday perspective, showing great value, and it resonated with the customer. We also had a really good pricing event.

I know our Kohl's Charge customer, we talked about the coupon eligibility had an effect on them, but just showing up with great prices also continues to benefit from a customer perspective. I said the third thing is we had some opportunities to really reinvest into depth. We've edited out choice and restored trip assurance with that customer, and that doesn't happen overnight, obviously, with inventory coming in, and I think we really showed up great throughout the quarter. We were able to build on that momentum. Particularly in those southern markets, I would say that we had opportunity to fill those in with more inventory, really when we talk about some of the small store strategies we've had.

Being able to bring them in inventory, they were actually able to really be productive with that investment and show strength, particularly in October, as that inventory was setting, all which sets us up, in my opinion, with good momentum as we lead into the fourth quarter. Clearly still had some weather headwinds in those cold weather categories, like Michael mentioned, where specifically in the North, you had outerwear and some fleece and sweaters that did see a slowdown as the weather warmed up. What I would say now is we're kind of seeing that cold weather come into play. We're definitely seeing a pickup in that business as well.

I would say that we were able to take advantage of the value orientation that we had centered around all year, the inventory depth that we had talked about restoring that trip assurance for the customer, and really that played through well into October and should build momentum into Q4.

Michael Binetti: Can I follow on that? Can we read that as you were able to deliver comps in third quarter that are within the range that you are guiding us to for fourth quarter without the benefit of weather? Can we interpret that as we are in the range today that you guided to for fourth quarter, or would weather turning be a source of upside? What can we read from your comments there? Thank you.

Jill Timm: Sure. I mean, my implied guide for Q4 was flat to up 2%, and right now, that means the midpoint is what we just finished on. So, I kind of feel like the low end is you have headwinds, whether that be macro or uncertainty or weather, and the high end continues to say that the momentum that we have talked about and the progress that we have put up this year continues, and the midpoint is right where we are at. So, that is how I would look at the guidance. Obviously, we have huge days ahead of us, Michael, which are going to be a big factor in the outcome of Q4.

But I believe, based on the strategy that we have employed, the momentum that we have seen, we are set up well to take advantage of those.

Michael Binetti: That is great. Thank you so much, Jill.

Operator: Your next question comes from the line of Blake Anderson with Jefferies. Your line is open. Please go ahead.

Blake Anderson: Hey, guys. Appreciate the question, and congrats on the great results and positive comp. Wanted to start with the commentary regarding trade-down. Curious if you can provide any color. Are these new customers? I believe you mentioned some higher income. Are they shopping more in-store or online? How are you ensuring you can maintain their spend over time as well, kind of on that trade-down dynamic? Then, Jill, I believe you mentioned the comp was more transaction-driven. Can you just talk about traffic conversion AUR, what you expect for Q4, and how should we think about the ability to drive higher AUR as well over time?

Jill Timm: Well, I would say in terms of the customer, when you're in a macro environment that we're navigating, we see a trade-down out of a higher income into our stores, and we need to take advantage of that. We can do that through the power of our national brands, like I mentioned. Nike, adidas, Levi's, all doing quite well for us in the quarter. That's an opportunity we have to introduce them into Kohl's. I think the elevation of our proprietary brands, showing them that we actually do have fashion and style in our stores, Sephora serves as a great anchor for that as well, are all opportunities for us to keep that customer in.

I think from a keeping that customer, we also see trade-offs in the middle, and that's where we're benefiting off of our proprietary brands right now. People have to make choices. They are definitely struggling in terms of where they're going to make payments with pressure and fuel and inflation. So, if we can give them a great product at a little bit lesser price point, that's where we see people making trade-offs, and that's where the power of the proprietary portfolio comes into play. Clearly, up 3.4% in the quarter, we saw that play out. In terms of the comp, we saw definitely it was driven both by transactions, which for us is an exciting pivot point.

We haven't been able to talk about transactions being positive in a while, so I think that's a big sentiment of positive growth. But also, we saw it in ATV, and that was more about the trade-offs that we just spoke about. Our units per transaction were up, offset with the lower AUR. I think this just goes to the fact that value is going to be incredibly important to this customer as we play out the rest of this holiday season. For us right now, we're focused on driving value, not so much expanding higher AURs.

I do believe when we're in a cycle that AURs are expanding, we have the right to play there, and we can do that through our national brands, like we talked about Nike, Sephora, and adidas. We can play in both spaces. Right now, I think for the customer, the most important thing is to deliver them value, and that's how we guided our Q4. I think that's what we would anticipate we will continue to do into 2027, unless we see a difference from an inflationary perspective. Obviously, we have opportunity to sharpen our pencils on 2027 and give you that guidance at the end of the year.

Michael J. Bender: Blake, the only other thing I would add, in addition to what Jill shared, is just the fact that from a consumer perspective, the importance of speed and convenience. You heard us talk about these initiated opportunities with DoorDash, Instacart, Klarna from a payment standpoint. Those are all pieces that factor into this value equation that our customer is working their way through as they're deciding where to shop, and the ability to get an item as quickly as possible, order it the way they want, have it show up quickly, and in some cases, pay for it over time with the support like Klarna.

Those are all things that we're adding into the mix to make sure that we're listening to what our customer is asking for from us to create that value equation that resonates most notably with them.

Blake Anderson: That's very helpful. Thanks so much.

Operator: We have reached the end of the Q&A session. This concludes today's call. Thank you for attending. You may now disconnect.
